text:
omar: Heads-up — ran a deploy-warmers experiment on prod-dedicated this morning. Goal: prefill KV prefixes for high-cardinality chat flows during a scale-up. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/boards/seed-salad :eyes:

sarah: link looks good. quick numbers? hit-rate + latency impact?

james: Raw summary: global kv_hitrate jumped from 38% -> 66% for seeded prefixes for the canary fleet, p50 token-cost down 12%, p99 latency improved ~85ms. BUT overall p99 for the cluster increased by ~30ms during the warmers run window (see notes).

michelle: Why did cluster p99 climb if seeded prefixes had better hit-rate?

james: Two main causes we profiled: (1) warmers created many concurrent small requests, spiking scheduling contention and increasing batching tail latency, (2) a kernel-selection regression for the quantized path meant the first few inference calls used a slower fallback kernel until the kernel cache warmed.

eve: For (1) the batcher logs show the max_batch_time was temporarily bumped to 40ms in the warmer controller to get stronger prefixes into one batch; that increases tail for unrelated live requests. We should cap warmer burst concurrency and prefer synthetic multi-token traces to fit normal batch windows.

omar: Agreed. Proposed changes before next run: 
- limit warmer concurrency per node to 4
- honour the live max_batch_time (dont override)
- route warmers to warm-only pods that have isolated batchers
- precompile / prime kernels on the node during deploy (see snippet)

james: Kernel-prime snippet we used (works on gpus with local FS cache):
```bash
# prime kernels for model X
for K in $(ls /models/x/kernels/*.ptx); do
  ./kernel_cache_populate --input-kernel $K --device cuda:0 || true
done
```
This reduced the quantized fallback time by ~45ms once the node had a populated kernel cache.

michelle: On keying: we noticed a regression after a change to prompt normalization. Normalization collapsed punctuation-only suffixes, merging distinct prefixes (samples below). That artificially raised warm-hit-rate but caused semantic collisions in production. Can we avoid normalization that drops entropy?

james: Example of problematic keying: 
- old key (raw): "User: Hi\nSystem: Summary:" + model + user_bucket
- new key (normalized): trimmed punctuation -> both "Hello?" and "Hello!!!" map to same key
Fix: include a stable hash of the raw prompt suffix as part of the KV key: `kv_key = prefix_id + model_v + raw_suffix_hash[0:8]`

omar: Good call. We should compute `raw_suffix_hash` with xxh3 to stay fast. Also add a tombstone TTL for keys created by warmers so they don't poison cache long-term.

eve: Synthetic traffic generator we used is in seed-salad. Quick config sample: 
```yaml
generator: seed-salad
rate: 50/s
trace_length: 12
prefix_sampling: top_k:1000, weight:0.8
user_bucket: stratified
```
It produces more realistic batching patterns than naive single-token pings.

deploy-bot: Canary warmers job started (job_id=seed-salad-1973009876), routing to nodes [n-12, n-13, n-14].

james: Experiment plan v2 (A/B):
- Group A: deploy-warmers with isolated warm-pods + kernel-prime pre-step + limited concurrency
- Group B: scheduled prefill job during low-traffic window (02:00–04:00) with synthetic traces, no kernel prime
Metrics: kv_hitrate (per-prefix), p50/p95/p99 generation latency, batch size distribution, scheduler queue depth, kernel-fallback-count, cost-per-token. Success criteria: +25–40% hit-rate on target prefixes, no >10ms cluster p99 regression, no >5% CPU/GPU scheduling spikes.

sarah: How long for the A/B run? 

michelle: 72h rolling canary, collect continuous traces + flamegraphs for slow tails. If any kernel-fallback spike >100/min or p99 regression >10ms sustained for 30m, auto-rollback.

omar: I'll kick off run A in 30m. ticket: ENG-RUN-871. Will post status updates.

infra-bot: Kernel prime completed on n-12 (14 kernels), n-13 pending, n-14 failed (OOM while populating).

omar: Noted the OOM on n-14 — lowering concurrent prime threads and retrying. Also adding an in-proc backoff if GPU memory > 80%.

james: One more observation: when batcher window shrinks under load, warm-hit-rate dips because warmers were tuned to longer sequences. We'll add adaptive warmers that sample observed seq_len distribution and emit traces that fit live batch shape.

michelle: Nice. That should reduce cross-talk between warmers and live traffic. After 72h we'll decide whether to make "warm-only" pods a permanent fleet.

sarah: :thumbsup: keep the short-status pings in this thread. Thanks team.

omar: Launching now. will update with metrics snapshot in ~2h.
